intro: Five stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Deadly Russian strike hits Zaporizhzhia region
items.text: Russian aerial bombs killed at least 26 people in the Zaporizhzhia region of Ukraine on Monday, according to the State Emergency Service. Two rescue workers and four police officers were among the dead, and five other people were injured. Governor Ivan Fedorov said Russian forces fired at least nine KAB-3000 bombs on the settlement of Komyshuvakha. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attack utterly horrific and said a second strike followed the first. He said it had dampened hopes of progress toward peace after a humanitarian operation in Oleshky.

gloss.aerial bomb: a bomb dropped from an aircraft
gloss.rescue worker: a person whose job is to save people in danger
gloss.settlement: a small place where people live
gloss.dampen: to make hopes or feelings weaker
gloss.humanitarian: connected with helping people who are suffering
gloss.double-tap strike: a second attack on the same place soon after the first

items.title: UK doubles wait for most migrants to settle
items.text: The British government set out new rules on Monday that will double the wait for many foreign workers who want to settle permanently. The qualifying period for indefinite leave to remain will rise from five years to ten for most workers. People earning more than £50,271 and some public service workers, including doctors, nurses and teachers, will still qualify after five years. Care workers earning £25,000 keep their five-year route. More than 200,000 people responded to the consultation. The rules are due to come into force next year and will not affect people who already have settled status.

gloss.set out: to explain a plan or idea clearly and in detail
gloss.settle: to make your permanent home in a country
gloss.indefinite leave to remain: the right to live in the UK with no time limit
gloss.qualifying period: the time you must wait before you are allowed to do something
gloss.consultation: a period when the public is asked for its opinions on a plan
gloss.come into force: to start to be official or to apply

items.title: Musetti beats Hurkacz in Paris tie-breaks
items.text: Lorenzo Musetti beat Hubert Hurkacz 7-6, 7-6 in the first round of the Paris Masters on Monday. The match lasted one hour and 43 minutes. Hurkacz saved three match points and held two set points in the second-set tie-break, but Musetti won it 12-10. Musetti now plays top seed Alexander Zverev, who had a first-round bye. Jannik Sinner is missing from the event because of a knee injury. A day earlier, Carlos Alcaraz had beaten Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 in the final of the Vienna Open.

gloss.tie-break: a short game used to decide a set that is level at six games each
gloss.match point: a point that would win the match for a player
gloss.seed: a player ranked highly and kept apart from other top players in the draw
gloss.bye: a free pass into the next round without playing
gloss.hold: to have, as in having a chance to win a set

items.title: GTA VI launch is two weeks away
items.text: Grand Theft Auto VI is due to be released on 19 November, according to GameRant. The game will come in a standard edition at $80 and an Ultimate Edition at $100. The Ultimate Edition includes extra content and exclusive access to certain in-game stores. Rockstar Games has built its marketing campaign gradually towards the launch. PlayStation's list of November releases also includes Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered on 3 November, Void/Breaker on 4 November and Barbie Rewind on 12 November.

gloss.edition: a particular version of a product, such as a game
gloss.exclusive: available only to a certain group of people
gloss.campaign: a planned set of actions to achieve a goal, such as selling a product
gloss.launch: the time when a new product first goes on sale
gloss.remastered: improved with better graphics or sound

items.title: Study: climate change may have halted an ice age
items.text: A new study suggests that human-driven climate change may have stopped a new ice age from starting. Researchers led by Young of the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory studied the Barnes Ice Cap, an area of about 6,000 square kilometres on Baffin Island in Canada. Using carbon-14 in plants near the edge of the glacier, they found that the Laurentide Ice Sheet was at its smallest about 3,000 years ago and began growing again around 2,000 years ago. The team argues that this growth should count as the start of the next ice age. They say the ice cap now loses more ice in summer than it gains in winter.

gloss.ice age: a long period when much of the Earth is covered in ice
gloss.ice cap: a large area of ice covering land
gloss.glacier: a large mass of ice that moves slowly
gloss.carbon-14: a form of carbon used to find out how old something is
gloss.argue: to give reasons to support an idea
